metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Egypt strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
Hey David, what do you think about buying some carnations for Tom? I heard they’re a classic gift for celebrations. 

Hmm... carnations, huh? They might be nice, but I wonder if there's something more meaningful. What do you think? 

I think they’re a safe choice. Plus, they symbolize admiration, which fits the occasion. But do you really think that buying flowers is enough to show our support? 

Well, it’s not just about the flowers. It’s about celebrating his achievement. Speaking of which, don’t you want to make your parents proud with your own success? 

I— I just don't see making my parents proud as one of my main goals in life. It's... complicated. 

Complicated how? Isn’t that a big part of why people strive for success? 

I mean, I get that for some people it is, but for me, it's different. I focus on my own path, not just meeting expectations. 

Fair enough, but flowers could still be a good way to express gratitude. What about a bouquet instead? 

Maybe... but I still feel like we should think outside the box. Something that really shows how much we appreciate him. 

Alright, let’s think of something more unique then. But back to the flowers, do you really think they wouldn't mean anything? 

Well, it's just that I don't want it to feel like just a formality. I guess we should find a way to make it personal.

That’s true, but I still think flowers can complement whatever we choose. They symbolize our appreciation and can be a meaningful part of the celebration. 

I suppose they could be. But do you think your parents would be proud of your contributions in this situation, even if it’s just about flowers? 

Absolutely! They’ve always taught me to honor relationships and celebrate achievements, no matter how small. It’s about showing respect.

shared_prefix.speaker: David

No, that's not how it works. In our way, success isn't just about making parents proud. Actually, many people in Japan focus on their own individual goals and not just adhering to the expectations of family. It’s a backward view to think that parental pride should dictate someone’s career path. 

I understand that perspective, but I think it’s important to recognize their sacrifices. It’s about honoring them while achieving your own dreams. 

Actually, that just seems naive. Properly speaking, success should stem from personal fulfillment, not a sense of duty to parents. It's about building your own identity.
